title: deploy conductor runbook & rollforward signal playlist (mar 2026) - sketch
content:
Goal: Provide a compact, operator-first runbook for a medium-risk model-serving change. Focus is on predictable ramp, quick detection, and fast rollforward/rollback decisions. This is a sketch intended for review; final will be condensed into templated checklists and a small UI deck for on-call handoff.

High-level assumptions:
- Change: runtime optimization + minor routing policy tweak (no model architecture changes).
- Expected impact: small latency improvement for 90th percentile; potential KCX incompatibility on rare long-seq requests.
- Target rollout: global, region-by-region, 48h window per region with micro-canary first 1%.

Preflight (72h before deploy)
- [ ] Merge-blocking PRs green, all tests pass (unit, integration, smoke).
- [ ] Canary harness built and validated against synthetic long-seq traffic.
- [ ] Perf benchmark snapshot taken (baseline): include p50/p90/p99, token/sec, memory footprint.
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards prepared: latency histogram, error counts by code, 99th tail KV cache hitrate, request length distribution.
- [ ] Alert gating reviewed with SRE: thresholds + action owners.
- [ ] QA signoff for canary scenarios + annotated sample prompts.
- [ ] Customer-impact list (whitelist of important tenants) verified and fallback policy scoped.
- [ ] Release notes draft created and linked to PR and Confluence.

T-minus 30m (pre-start checklist)
- [ ] Slack: #release-ops notified with timeframe and on-call roster.
- [ ] PagerDuty bridge created: "Deploy Conductor - <region>" with 1h auto-ack window.
- [ ] DB/Schema: no migration. Confirmed.
- [ ] Infra capacity reserve: +10% headroom in region for warmup.
- [ ] Backout artifact ready (exact config commit hash).

Rollout calendar (example, Europe region)
- Hour 0: push canary variant at 1% traffic for 30 minutes.
  - Quick smoke: sample requests from canary_sanity_suite; verify responses contain expected tool call markers and token counts.
  - Gate: if error rate > 0.5% OR p99 latency increase > 25% -> immediate rollback to baseline and escalate.
- Hour 0-2: monitor, extend canary to 5% if green.
  - Add watchlist: top 10 tenants by QPS, auth-failed log spikes, degraded embedding scores.
- Hour 2-6: stagger to 20% if telemetry stable for 2h.
  - Gate: KV-cache hitrate no worse than -5% relative to baseline; tail lat increase < 15%
- Hour 6-24: linear ramp to 60% with 3-hour holds and automated healthchecks.
- Hour 24-48: full 100% if no gating failures; otherwise fallback to safe variant and prepare for further investigation.

Decision gates and thresholds (suggested)
- Stop/rollback gates (any triggers require immediate rollback and incident channel):
  - Increase in user-facing errors > 0.5% above baseline sustained for 5 minutes.
  - P99 latency increase > 40% sustained for 10 minutes.
  - Unhandled exceptions spike > 10x baseline for 2 minutes.
  - Authentication/authorization failures affecting > 0.1% of requests.
- Pause gates (operator review required):
  - P99 latency increase between 25-40% or error increase between 0.2-0.5%.
  - Observed degradation in quality signals tied to prompt set (e.g., rerank drop > 3 points).

Rollback matrix (quick reference)
- Fast rollback: re-route traffic to previous config/variant, rollforward flag disabled. Target RT: < 2 minutes.
- Staged rollback: reduce to safe variant then incrementally reintroduce features one at a time.
- Hot patch: if rollback not possible (config frozen), deploy a hotfix with targeted instrumentation and canary.

Observability playbook (what to watch)
- Primary dashboards: request-latency-by-model, errors-by-code, kv-cache-hitrate, tokens-per-request, downstream-backpressure.
- Traces: sample from p99 requests; check for unexpected CPU spin/wait in kernel selection.
- Logs: search for "kv-miss:long-seq" and "kernel-select-fallback" patterns.
- Quality checks: run evaluation harness against golden prompt set every 30 minutes during ramp.

Communication templates
- Slack (initial): "Starting deploy conductor -> eu-west1 at 09:00 UTC. Canary 1% for 30m. PD bridge: <link>. On-call: Aisha, Marco, Dana. Watch latency and errors."
- Slack (on gate hit): ":warning: Gate hit (p99 latency 42% up). Rolling back to baseline and standing up postmortem channel."
- Release notes excerpt (to be published after final 100%): "Runtime selection optimization + routing policy tweak. Expected p90 latency improvement ~8%. No model changes. See post-deploy metrics at confluence link."

Post-release checklist (first 48h)
- [ ] 4h, 12h, 24h, 48h stability checks: verify error budget, latency, and top-tenant KPIs.
- [ ] Sweep logs for backpressure signs and secondary effects (e.g., increased downstream retries).
- [ ] Capture perf delta and update model catalog performance entry.
- [ ] Customer comms if any high-impact tenant observed.
- [ ] Postmortem slot reserved on calendar if any gate tripped.

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide if canary should be traffic-shared across regions (multi-region canary) or strictly regionalized (operational simplicity vs signal).
- Finalize auto-escalation thresholds with SRE (tuning for weekday vs weekend).
- Add automated golden-prompt quality regression smoke that runs preflight and during canary step.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally operator-centric; we prefer short checkboxes and explicit gating thresholds rather than long prose.
- If we accept these thresholds, I'll convert them to the UI rollout wizard and add minimal scripts to automate gate evaluations.

Quick references:
- Canary PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/6782
- Perf baseline: confluence:perf-benchmarks-2026-03-17
- On-call rota: https://redwood.atlassian.net/people/rota

Acknowledgements: Marco ran the initial stress harness, Dana validated the alert curves, Omar did the sample prompt suite.

Last edited by: Aisha Patel

----
Editorial note: keep this sketch lightweight and actionable. We'll fold into the release-runbook template once this iteration proves clean in a dry-run.
